definitions.explanation: Describes saying things straight out with no regard for how they will land. Usually critical of the speaker's tactlessness, though it can be said admiringly of someone brave enough to speak up.

examples.japanese: ⟦{初対面|しょたいめん}→初対面：07306_shotaimen⟧な⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ずけずけ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{年齢|ねんれい}→年齢：01490_nenrei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}かれた→聞く：00483_kiku⟧。
examples.english: Even though we had just met, I was bluntly asked my age.
Being able to speak his mind bluntly even to his boss is also one of his good points.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
- Used as ずけずけ(⟦と→と：00512_to⟧) before a verb of speaking; the ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧ is optional but common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ずけずけ⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧: to speak bluntly
- ずけずけ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{物|もの}→物：02259_mono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧: to say things without mincing words
- ずけずけ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{聞|き}く→聞く：00483_kiku⟧: to ask something point-blank

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦はっきり→はっきり：01228_hakkiri⟧: clearly — states things plainly, with no suggestion of rudeness
- ⟦{率直|そっちょく}→率直：13491_socchoku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: frankly — a positive word for the same directness

ずけずけ is nearly always about what someone else does; describing your own speech that way sounds boastful or self-deprecating rather than neutral.
